practiceQuestions.q: Which article of the Indian Constitution provides for the office of the Deputy Speaker of the Lok Sabha?
practiceQuestions.sol: Article 93 of the Indian Constitution mandates that the House of the People shall, as soon as may be, choose two members of the House to be respectively Speaker and Deputy Speaker thereof.

practiceQuestions.q: Who elects the Deputy Speaker of the Lok Sabha?
opts: The Lok Sabha from amongst its members
The Speaker of the Lok Sabha alone
Both Houses of Parliament in a joint sitting
practiceQuestions.sol: The Deputy Speaker is elected by the Lok Sabha itself from amongst its members. Once the office of the Deputy Speaker falls vacant, the House chooses another member to fill the vacancy.

practiceQuestions.q: To whom does the Deputy Speaker of the Lok Sabha submit their resignation?
opts: The Speaker of the Lok Sabha
The Secretary-General of the Lok Sabha
practiceQuestions.sol: Under Article 94(b), the Deputy Speaker of the Lok Sabha resigns by writing under their hand addressed to the Speaker of the Lok Sabha.

practiceQuestions.q: What is the normal tenure of the Deputy Speaker of the Lok Sabha?
opts: As long as they enjoy the pleasure of the President
Co-terminus with the life of the Lok Sabha (unless they cease to be a member)
practiceQuestions.sol: The Deputy Speaker holds office until they cease to be a member of the House, resigns, or is removed by a resolution passed by a majority of all the then members of the House.

practiceQuestions.q: When presiding over a sitting of the House, does the Deputy Speaker have the right to vote in the first instance?
opts: No, they can only exercise a casting vote in the case of a tie
Yes, but only on Money Bills
No, they never have any voting rights under any circumstances
practiceQuestions.sol: Like the Speaker, the Deputy Speaker does not vote in the first instance when presiding. They exercise a casting vote only in the event of a tie (equality of votes).

practiceQuestions.q: Who was the first Deputy Speaker of independent India's Lok Sabha?
practiceQuestions.sol: M. Ananthasayanam Ayyangar was elected as the first Deputy Speaker of the Lok Sabha in independent India, serving under Speaker G. V. Mavalankar.

practiceQuestions.q: By what majority must a resolution for the removal of the Deputy Speaker be passed in the Lok Sabha?
opts: Simple majority of members present and voting
All then members of the House (Effective Majority)
Two-thirds of total membership of the House
practiceQuestions.sol: Under Article 94(c), the Deputy Speaker may be removed from office by a resolution of the House passed by a majority of all the then members of the House (effective majority), after giving 14 days' notice.

practiceQuestions.q: What is the mandatory notice period required before moving a resolution for the removal of the Deputy Speaker?
practiceQuestions.sol: A resolution for the removal of the Speaker or Deputy Speaker can only be moved if a notice of at least 14 days has been given of the intention to move the resolution.

practiceQuestions.q: When the office of the Speaker is vacant, who performs the duties of the Speaker?
practiceQuestions.sol: Under Article 95(1), while the office of Speaker is vacant, the duties of the office shall be performed by the Deputy Speaker or, if the office of Deputy Speaker is also vacant, by such member of the Lok Sabha as the President may appoint.

practiceQuestions.q: Is the Deputy Speaker subordinate to the Speaker of the Lok Sabha?
opts: Yes, the Speaker exercises administrative control over the Deputy Speaker
No, the Deputy Speaker is not subordinate to the Speaker; they are independently elected by the House
Yes, the Speaker appoints the Deputy Speaker
No, because the Deputy Speaker is appointed by the President
practiceQuestions.sol: The Deputy Speaker is not subordinate to the Speaker. They derive their powers directly from the Constitution and the Rules of Procedure of the Lok Sabha, and are responsible to the House, not the Speaker.

practiceQuestions.q: How does the parliamentary convention regarding the election of the Deputy Speaker evolved in India differ from the British House of Commons tradition?
opts: In India, the Deputy Speaker is always chosen from the ruling party, whereas in Britain they belong to the opposition.

By convention in recent decades in India, the post of Deputy Speaker has often been offered to the opposition, mirroring the healthy British convention of bipartisan consensus, though statutory mandates differ.
Britain has no Deputy Speaker, unlike India.
In Britain, the Deputy Speaker is appointed by the Monarch without election.
practiceQuestions.sol: While the Constitution provides for the election of the Deputy Speaker, a healthy convention developed in India where the post went to the opposition (similar to the UK where the Deputy Speaker often comes from the opposition parties to ensure neutrality), though recent parliaments have seen friction on this convention.

practiceQuestions.q: What constitutional implication arises if both the offices of the Speaker and the Deputy Speaker of the Lok Sabha fall vacant simultaneously?
opts: The Lok Sabha is automatically dissolved.
The President appoints a member of the Lok Sabha to perform the duties of the Speaker under Article 95(1).
The Chief Justice of India assumes the role of Lok Sabha Speaker.
The senior-most Union Cabinet Minister presides over the House.
practiceQuestions.sol: Article 95(1) explicitly states that if both offices are vacant, the duties of the Speaker shall be performed by such member of the Lok Sabha as the President may appoint for the purpose.

practiceQuestions.q: When the Deputy Speaker presides over a meeting of a Parliamentary Committee of which they are a member, what is their status?
opts: They cannot vote on any committee matters.
By virtue of being Deputy Speaker, they automatically become the chairman of all such committees.

If the Deputy Speaker is a member of a parliamentary committee, they are appointed as the chairman of that committee by convention/rules if they are a member, or they act as chairman if nominated/ex-officio provisions apply.
The Deputy Speaker cannot be a member of any Parliamentary Committee.
practiceQuestions.sol: Under parliamentary rules, whenever the Deputy Speaker is a member of a Parliamentary Committee, they are invariably appointed as the Chairman of that committee (e.g., Committee on Private Members' Bills and Resolutions).

practiceQuestions.q: Why has the non-election or delay in electing a Deputy Speaker in recent Lok Sabhas become a point of judicial and political debate in India?
opts: Because Article 93 uses the mandatory word 'shall', implying that choosing a Deputy Speaker is a constitutional imperative rather than a matter of political discretion.
Because the Supreme Court has the power to directly appoint the Deputy Speaker if the House fails to do so within 30 days.
Because without a Deputy Speaker, Money Bills cannot be passed.
Because the Deputy Speaker's salary is paid from the Contingency Fund of India directly.
practiceQuestions.sol: Article 93 states that the House 'shall' choose a Deputy Speaker as soon as may be. Legal experts and public interest litigations have argued that keeping this constitutional post vacant violates the mandatory spirit of the Constitution.

practiceQuestions.q: Does the Deputy Speaker have any special administrative powers distinct from ordinary members of the Lok Sabha when not presiding?
opts: Yes, they automatically head the Lok Sabha Secretariat.
No, when not presiding, they enjoy the same rights, privileges, and immunities as any other ordinary Member of Parliament.
They possess veto power over bills passed by the Rajya Sabha.
practiceQuestions.sol: When not occupying the chair, the Deputy Speaker is an ordinary MP. They do not possess independent executive or administrative powers over the Secretariat unless performing specific delegated duties or presiding.

practiceQuestions.q: When the Speaker is present in the House, what is the status of the Deputy Speaker?
opts: They sit next to the Speaker on the dais.
They sit on the floor of the House like any other member and can participate in debates and vote.
They act as the Leader of the House.
They must remain outside the Parliament chamber.
practiceQuestions.sol: When the Speaker is presiding, the Deputy Speaker sits in the House as an ordinary member, taking part in discussions, raising questions, and casting votes like any other MP.

practiceQuestions.q: Which of the following best describes the accountability of the Deputy Speaker?
opts: Accountable to the President of India
Accountable to the Lok Sabha and removable by a resolution of the House
Accountable to the Speaker of the Lok Sabha
Accountable to the Supreme Court of India
practiceQuestions.sol: The Deputy Speaker is elected by the Lok Sabha and can be removed by the Lok Sabha. Thus, their institutional accountability is directly to the House of the People.

practiceQuestions.q: Is a Deputy Speaker, upon election, required to resign from their political party?
opts: Yes, it is a mandatory constitutional requirement under the Anti-Defection Law.

No, unlike the British Speaker who severs all party ties, Indian Speakers and Deputy Speakers traditionally do not formally resign from their political parties, though they are expected to act impartially.
Yes, by convention established by the Election Commission.
No, and they are allowed to campaign for their party while presiding.
practiceQuestions.sol: Unlike the UK where the Speaker cuts all party affiliations, in India, Speakers and Deputy Speakers do not formally resign from their parties, though high standards of parliamentary impartiality are expected while in the chair.

practiceQuestions.q: What happens to the Deputy Speaker's membership of the Lok Sabha if the House is dissolved prematurely?
opts: They immediately lose their membership of the Lok Sabha and office of Deputy Speaker.
They cease to hold office only when the newly elected Lok Sabha meets, ensuring continuity of the office.
They continue as Deputy Speaker for another 5 years irrespective of dissolution.
They are automatically elevated to the position of Speaker.
practiceQuestions.sol: Unlike the Speaker, whose office does not vacate immediately upon dissolution of the Lok Sabha (they vacate only immediately before the first meeting of the newly elected House), the Deputy Speaker's office continues under the proviso to Article 94 until the newly elected Lok Sabha meets.

practiceQuestions.q: Can the Deputy Speaker preside over a joint sitting of both Houses of Parliament?
opts: Yes, always in the absence of the Speaker.
No, the Constitution specifies that the Speaker presides over joint sittings, and in their absence, the Deputy Chairman of the Rajya Sabha, not the Deputy Speaker of the Lok Sabha.
Yes, if approved by the President of India.
Only if the Rajya Sabha Chairman permits.
practiceQuestions.sol: Under Article 118(4), joint sittings are presided over by the Speaker. Under Rule 3 of the Houses of Parliament (Joint Sittings and Communications) Rules, if the Speaker is absent, the Deputy Speaker of the Lok Sabha does NOT automatically preside; rather, the Deputy Chairman of the Rajya Sabha takes the chair, followed by the Vice-Chairman of the Rajya Sabha or other specified persons.

practiceQuestions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding the Deputy Speaker of the Lok Sabha:
1. The election of the Deputy Speaker is mandated by Article 93 of the Constitution of India.
2. The date of election of the Deputy Speaker is fixed by the President of India.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
practiceQuestions.sol: Statement 1 is correct: Article 93 provides for the election of both the Speaker and Deputy Speaker. Statement 2 is incorrect: The date of election of the Speaker is fixed by the President, but the date of election of the Deputy Speaker is fixed by the *Speaker* of the Lok Sabha.

practiceQuestions.q:
Consider the following statements:
1. The Deputy Speaker has the same powers as the Speaker when presiding over a sitting of the Lok Sabha.
2. An appeal against a ruling given by the Deputy Speaker can be made to the Speaker of the Lok Sabha.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
practiceQuestions.sol: Statement 1 is incorrect because while the Deputy Speaker exercises identical powers while presiding, Article 95(2) states that the Deputy Speaker acts 'when presiding' under specific rules, and certain institutional powers of the Speaker (like certifying a Money Bill under Article 110) cannot be performed by the Deputy Speaker unless the Speaker's office is vacant and they are performing the duties of the Speaker. Statement 2 is incorrect because the Speaker does not sit as an appellate authority over rulings given by the Deputy Speaker; rulings from the Chair (whether by Speaker, Deputy Speaker, or Panel of Chairpersons) are final and cannot be appealed.

practiceQuestions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding the removal of the Deputy Speaker:
1. A resolution for removal can be moved only with the prior approval of the President.
2. The Deputy Speaker cannot preside over a meeting of the House while a resolution for their own removal is under consideration.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
practiceQuestions.sol: Statement 1 is incorrect: No presidential approval is required to move a removal resolution against the Deputy Speaker; it requires only a 14-day notice and support of members. Statement 2 is correct: Under Article 96(2), the Deputy Speaker shall not preside while a resolution for their removal from office is under consideration.

practiceQuestions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding the voting rights of the Deputy Speaker:
1. The Deputy Speaker has the right to vote on all matters in the House when they are not presiding.
2. When presiding, the Deputy Speaker can vote in the first instance to break a deadlock.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
practiceQuestions.sol: Statement 1 is correct: As an ordinary member of the Lok Sabha when not presiding, the Deputy Speaker has the right to vote on bills, resolutions, and motions. Statement 2 is incorrect: When presiding, the Deputy Speaker cannot vote in the first instance; they only exercise a casting vote in the event of an equality of votes.

practiceQuestions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding the Speaker and Deputy Speaker:
1. Both offices derive their authority from Chapter II of Part V of the Constitution of India.
2. Both officers vacate their offices immediately if they cease to be members of the Lok Sabha.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
practiceQuestions.sol: Both statements are correct. Articles 93 to 97 relating to the Officers of Parliament (Speaker and Deputy Speaker) fall under Chapter II (Parliament) of Part V of the Constitution. Furthermore, Article 94(a) explicitly states that both the Speaker and Deputy Speaker vacate their office if they cease to be members of the House.

practiceQuestions.q:
Consider the following statements about the salary and allowances of the Deputy Speaker:
1. They are determined by Parliament by law and charged upon the Consolidated Fund of India.
2. Their salary can be reduced during a Financial Emergency proclaimed under Article 360.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
practiceQuestions.sol: Both statements are correct. Under Article 97, salaries and allowances of the Speaker and Deputy Speaker are fixed by Parliament and charged upon the Consolidated Fund of India. Under Article 360, during a Financial Emergency, provisions can be made for the reduction of salaries and allowances of all or any class of persons serving the Union, including holders of constitutional offices like the Speaker and Deputy Speaker.

practiceQuestions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding the role of the Deputy Speaker under Article 96:
1. The Deputy Speaker has the right to speak and to take part in the proceedings of the Lok Sabha while a resolution for their removal from office is under consideration.
2. They are entitled to vote on the resolution for their removal in the first instance.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
practiceQuestions.sol: Statement 1 is correct: Article 96(2) explicitly provides that the Speaker or Deputy Speaker shall have the right to speak in, and otherwise to take part in the proceedings of, the House while any resolution for their removal is under consideration. Statement 2 is incorrect: Article 96(2) specifies that they shall have the right to vote *only in the first instance* on such resolution (not a casting vote), but do not have a casting vote during this specific proceeding because they are not presiding.

practiceQuestions.q:
Consider the following statements concerning the Panel of Chairpersons and the Deputy Speaker:
1. The Deputy Speaker is one of the members of the Panel of Chairpersons nominated by the Speaker.
2. Unlike members of the Panel of Chairpersons, the Deputy Speaker is a constitutional officer elected by the House.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
practiceQuestions.sol: Statement 1 is incorrect: The Deputy Speaker is NOT a member of the Panel of Chairpersons. The Speaker nominates a panel of not more than 10 members from among Lok Sabha MPs to preside in the absence of both the Speaker and Deputy Speaker. Statement 2 is correct: The Deputy Speaker is a distinct constitutional office under Article 93, elected directly by the House.

practiceQuestions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding constitutional provisions and parliamentary practices associated with the Deputy Speaker:
1. The Constitution explicitly mandates that the Deputy Speaker shall belong to the opposition party.
2. The resignation of the Deputy Speaker takes effect immediately upon being written and addressed to the Speaker, without requiring acceptance by the Speaker.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
practiceQuestions.sol: Statement 1 is incorrect: The Constitution contains no provision requiring the Deputy Speaker to be from the opposition; it is purely a matter of parliamentary convention. Statement 2 is correct: Under Article 94(b), writing under their hand addressed to the Speaker constitutes a valid resignation which takes effect immediately upon submission, requiring no formal acceptance by the recipient.

practiceQuestions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding the financial and administrative privileges of the Deputy Speaker:
1. The salary and allowances of the Deputy Speaker are subject to annual vote of the Parliament.
2. The conduct of the Deputy Speaker in relation to the regulation of procedure or maintenance of order in the Lok Sabha is subject to the jurisdiction of any court.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
practiceQuestions.sol: Both statements are incorrect. Statement 1 is incorrect because the salary and allowances of the Deputy Speaker are 'charged' upon the Consolidated Fund of India and are non-votable by Parliament (though their amount is fixed by law made by Parliament). Statement 2 is incorrect because under Article 122, the validity of any proceedings in Parliament shall not be called in question on the ground of any alleged irregularity of procedure, and parliamentary officers (including the Deputy Speaker) enjoy immunity from court jurisdiction for exercising powers to regulate procedure or maintain order.
